Findings

Requests are failing failerror_rate−30 grade pointseffort 0.5–3 days

15 of 24 requests failed (HTTP 429 ×15)

Every failed request is either a user-visible error or a retry that costs latency and money. The status breakdown in the evidence says whether it is rate limiting, timeouts or server errors.

Fix: For 429s, raise the rate limit or add client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter. For timeouts, compare the request timeout with the measured request duration. For 5xx, read the server logs at the times of the scan.

Failures rise at the highest concurrency failerror_rate_at_peak−30 grade pointseffort 1–3 days

5 of 8 requests failed at concurrency 4

The endpoint refuses or drops requests once enough arrive together, which is exactly when traffic peaks.

Fix: Size capacity or rate limits for the concurrency your traffic reaches, and make the client back off on 429 and 503 rather than retrying immediately.

No Prometheus metrics at /metrics warnmetrics_endpoint−5 grade pointseffort 0.5 days

no Prometheus exposition answered at /metrics on the target's origin

Queue depth, batch size and cache usage are what explain a latency problem. Without them, a slowdown can be seen but not diagnosed.

Fix: Enable the server's metrics endpoint (llama.cpp needs `--metrics`; vLLM and TGI serve /metrics by default) and scrape it. If the endpoint sits behind a gateway, expose the metrics there.

Tokvera contacts only the target you specify, plus GitHub when you run update or doctor --check-update, and tokvera.halotrcer.com and GitHub for the plugin's first-run install.

The load used Tokvera's fixed, harmless benchmark prompts. Response text was read for timing and discarded; none is stored in this report.

critical Hard-coded Slack tokenSEC001deal risk

custom · testdata/scan/cursor-mcp.json · server slack · env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN

Evidence (masked): xoxb… (28 chars)

A credential is written in the configuration file, readable by anything that can read the file and copied into backups and dotfile repositories.

Fix: Move it to the environment or a secret store and reference it (for example ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}); then rotate it, since it has been on disk.

high Literal value in secret-named field X-API-KeySEC002deal risk

custom · testdata/scan/vscode-mcp.jsonc · server api · headers.X-API-Key

Evidence (masked): lite… (21 chars)

The field's name says it holds a credential, and its value is written in the file rather than referenced.

Fix: Reference it from the environment (for example ${X_API_KEY}) and rotate it.

high Credential embedded in the server URLSEC004deal risk

custom · testdata/scan/cursor-mcp.json · server cap-remote · url

Evidence (masked): https://mcp.capability.example/apps/{masked:22}/mcp

The URL itself grants access (path segment 2 (high-entropy)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.

Fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.

high Credential embedded in the server URLSEC004deal risk

custom · testdata/scan/cursor-mcp.json · server notes · url

Evidence (masked): https://mcp.example.com/sse{masked:16}

The URL itself grants access (query api_key (token query key)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.

Fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.

medium Server runs with all permissions (Deno)PERM003

custom · testdata/scan/cursor-mcp.json · server deno · args[1]

Evidence (masked): --allow-all

The server can reach far more than its tools need, which widens what a compromised or manipulated server can do.

Fix: Grant only the access the server needs (for Deno, --allow-net=<hosts>; for containers, a dedicated network).

Tool descriptions, and the resources and prompts each server offers, were not checked: that needs starting the servers (sievant scan --inspect-tools, which runs them).

Gateway coverage (sievant report, 30d)

unknown · controls enforced 7 of 12 · 0 requests, 0 blocked.

high No audit trail to report on

Fix: Run Sievant (sievant proxy through sievant wrap, or sievant serve) so it records calls, and point --audit at its store.

medium Wrapped servers allow every tool

Fix: Write a configuration (sievant init --profile balanced or strict), let it observe, then narrow it with sievant policy suggest and apply.

low Suspected prompt injection is recorded, not acted on

Fix: Set injection.action to annotate (the injection pack) or block for the agents that need it.

low Personal data in tool arguments is passed on

Fix: Set sanitization.input_pii to redact or block (pack secrets-pii).

info MCP client configurations were not checked

Fix: Run sievant report without --no-clients, or sievant scan.

How to read this report

Halotrcer's ranking across the two tools is provisional (scoring version 0.1.0): its tiers are judgement, not calibrated. See docs/scoring.md.

Halotrcer contacts only the target you give it (through Tokvera) and reads only the MCP configuration files Sievant reads, on this machine. It sends no telemetry. Secrets stay masked as each tool masks them; on top of that, Halotrcer drops URL credentials and query strings, hides environment values, shows your home directory as ~ and replaces your user name with <user>.
